title: Ministers of State (Checks for Security Purposes) Bill 2019
short_title: Ministers of State (Checks for Security Purposes) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require security background checks for federal ministers, assistant ministers and parliamentary secretaries.
The Director-General of Security would provide reports to the Prime Minister on any security issues arising from a minister's personal background.
The bill would address a gap in Australia's Protective Security Framework by removing the current exemption that allows ministers to access classified information without security clearance.
changes: Requires the Director-General of Security to conduct comprehensive background checks on ministers.
Provides the Prime Minister with security reports on ministers without overriding the Prime Minister's appointment decisions.
Closes a gap in the security framework that currently exempts ministers from clearance processes.
summary.affected: Ministers of State, including Cabinet Ministers, other Ministers, Assistant Ministers and Parliamentary Secretaries.

divisions.question: The majority voted against a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2019-07-29.3.2) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill [for a second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/learning/fact-sheets/making-a-law.html). ### What did the bill do? The [bill](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/Bills_Search_Results/Result?bId=s1175) was introduced to: > *[require] the Prime Minister to direct the Director-General of Security to provide a report on matters relating to security arising from examination of the personal background and circumstances of all current and future ministers of state.*
